W1.name: Ines Okafor
W1.text: Ines Okafor was the only passenger on the ferry, a newcomer to the island who had been appointed by the council as the new keeper of the Salt Ledger.
W1.quote: Keeper of the Salt Ledger," Ines said.

W2.name: Tobiah Wren
W2.text: Tobiah Wren was the old ferryman who carried Ines to Harrow Quay; his left thumb was missing, and he had known the previous keeper.
W2.quote: The ferryman was an old man named Tobiah Wren.

W3.name: Aldous Brandt
W3.text: Aldous Brandt was the previous keeper of the Salt Ledger, who kept it for thirty years and had been gone three weeks.

W4.name: Harrow Quay
W4.text: Harrow Quay was the island port, with a grey harbour wall, smokehouses and a white tower called the Lamp House, reached by ferry from the mainland.
W4.quote: a grey harbour wall, a row of smokehouses

G1.text: Ines Okafor was to keep the Salt Ledger as the new keeper, and Tobiah Wren told her to keep the brass key off the ledger and hidden from the council.
G1.quote: Do not show it to the council.

E1.text: Tobiah Wren told Ines Okafor that Aldous Brandt had not left on his ferry, contradicting the printed claim that Brandt had gone to the mainland.
E1.quote: I carry everyone who leaves this island, and I did not carry him.

E2.text: Tobiah Wren gave Ines Okafor a small brass key with a fish-shaped bow that Aldous Brandt had given him for whoever kept the book next.
E2.quote: It was a small brass key, no longer than her finger

E3.text: Tobiah Wren left Ines on the quay and sailed north to the cod banks, saying he would not return before the equinox.
E3.quote: would not return before the equinox

Q1.text: What happened to Aldous Brandt, who Tobiah Wren says did not leave by ferry, was left unanswered.
Q1.quote: A man like that does not walk away from his desk.

Q2.text: What the brass key opens, the 'door that isn't a door' according to Aldous Brandt, was not stated.
Q2.quote: He said it was for a door that isn't a door

W5.name: Mara Venn
W5.text: Mara Venn was the tall, grey-haired harbourmaster of Harrow Quay, who wore the town seal on a cord and showed Ines the Salt Ledger.

W6.name: Anselm Pike
W6.text: Anselm Pike was the round, cheerful physician and printer of Harrow Quay, who had played chess with Aldous Brandt every Thursday for eleven years.
W6.quote: I am the physician here, and also the printer

G2.text: Ines Okafor was to finish the audit of the Salt Ledger before the equinox market, so the island could refuse the Crane Company's offer.
G2.quote: The council needs the audit finished before the equinox market,

E4.text: Mara Venn explained that the Crane Company had offered to buy the island's fishing rights, and that if the debts were not settled and the book clean, half the quay's houses would have to sell.
E4.quote: If it is not, half the houses on this quay will have to sell.

E5.text: Ines Okafor found that the Salt Ledger's pages between February and June had been torn out, leaving only stubs, and Mara Venn said the book was found like that the morning Brandt was gone.
E5.quote: Between February and June there was nothing but a row of torn stubs.

E6.text: Anselm Pike brought Ines Okafor soup and said Aldous Brandt was not the sort to leave, though people surprise us.
E6.quote: He was not the sort to leave,

Q3.text: Who tore the spring pages out of the Salt Ledger, and why, was left unanswered; Mara Venn said some claim Brandt took them but that she knew nothing.
Q3.quote: Some say he took them with him.

Q4.text: What the locked tide-clock on the landing below the archive is, and whether it matters, was left unexplained.
Q4.quote: an old tide-clock set into the wall, its brass case locked

W7.name: Mara Lisle
W7.text: Mara Lisle was a girl of about nineteen who mended trawls in the net loft and had run Brandt's errands since she was twelve; she shares a first name with harbourmaster Mara Venn.
W7.quote: Mara Lisle had run Brandt's errands since she was twelve.

E7.text: Mara Lisle told Ines Okafor that in his last month Aldous Brandt stopped sleeping and went to the salt warehouse at night, counting barrels and returning with chalk on his sleeves.
E7.quote: He went down to the salt warehouse at night with a lantern and came back with chalk on his sleeves.

E8.text: Mara Lisle relayed Brandt's saying that a book can be honest in every line and still tell a lie, which reminded Ines of her mother's chandlery books burning in Port Selby.
E8.quote: He only said that a book can be honest in every line and still tell a lie.

E9.text: Ines Okafor found an unsigned note under the archive door, marked with a drawn seabird and signed the Cormorant, saying the spring pages were not burned; she locked it in her trunk and told no one.
E9.quote: "The spring pages are not burned," the note said.

Q5.text: Who the Cormorant is, and why they sent Ines the note, was left unanswered.
Q5.quote: "Count the salt, not the fish. — the Cormorant"

Q6.text: Why Aldous Brandt was counting barrels in the salt warehouse at night, and what he found, was not stated.

G3.text: Ines Okafor tried to get the sealed salt warehouse opened so she could count the barrels on the floor, and was told to bring a council order.
G3.quote: asked the harbourmaster to open the salt warehouse

E10.text: Ines Okafor counted the salt over four days and found the ledger recorded forty barrels a month while the carters' receipts showed sixty-four, so twenty-four barrels monthly never reached the book.
E10.quote: Twenty-four barrels a month had come onto the island and never reached the book.

E11.text: Mara Venn refused to open the salt warehouse without a council order, saying it was sealed until the market; Ines grew angry and began to wonder whether the seal-holder was the one she sought.
E11.quote: "Not without an order from the council," Mara Venn said.

E12.text: A second note from the Cormorant appeared under Ines's door, saying the harbourmaster signs what she is given and telling Ines to ask who writes the tide tables.
E12.quote: The harbourmaster signs what she is given.

Q7.text: Who writes the tide tables, and why the Cormorant pointed Ines to them, was left unanswered.
Q7.quote: Ask who writes the tide tables.

Q8.text: Who is moving the unrecorded twenty-four barrels of salt a month, and to whom the cured fish is sold, was not stated.
Q8.quote: Whoever was moving it unseen was curing fish that no one had recorded

G4.text: Ines Okafor meant to carry her copied salt tally to the council in the morning.
G4.quote: She meant to carry this tally to the council in the morning.

E13.text: Ines Okafor learned from the baker that the tide tables were printed on the island's only press, which stood in the back room of Dr Pike's dispensary, and she did not go to Pike.
E13.quote: the press stood in the back room of Dr Pike's dispensary

E14.text: Ines copied her salt count onto a single sheet showing forty barrels in the book against sixty-four on the receipts, month by month.
E14.quote: she copied her salt count onto a single sheet

E15.text: Near midnight an unseen intruder climbed the tower, the archive lamp went out, and the intruder took Ines's tally while leaving the ledger and the receipts untouched.
E15.quote: The tally was gone from the desk.

Q9.text: Who entered the archive in the dark and took only the tally, and why, was left unanswered; Ines noticed a smell of tar and juniper she almost knew.
Q9.quote: She did not know who had stood beside her in the dark

G5.text: Ines Okafor decided to keep the receipts tin hidden on her person instead of handing it to Dr Pike, after concluding that the man who prints the tide tables is the one to distrust.
G5.quote: Ines put the biscuit tin under her coat and did not take it to the dispensary.

E16.text: Dr Anselm Pike found Ines on the tower steps, heard her story, hinted that Mara Venn's coat smelled of tar and juniper, and asked for the receipts tin to keep in his dispensary strongbox.

E17.text: Ines saw that the printed tide table said midnight's tide was lowest, though she had seen high water at the quay rings at midnight, so the table was false.
E17.quote: the water had been high against the quay, right up to the iron rings.

E18.text: Ines reasoned that a false low-tide table would keep watchers from the harbour when a boat could land, and that only one man printed the tables, so she withheld the tin from Pike.
E18.quote: nobody would look at the harbour at the one hour when a boat could come in.

Q10.text: Whether Pike's hint about Mara Venn's coat is true, or an attempt to misdirect Ines, was left unanswered.
Q10.quote: But you have met our harbourmaster's coat.

G6.text: Ines Okafor and Mara Lisle set out to find the hidden spring pages by trying the brass key in the one case Ines had never tried.
G6.quote: she thought of the one brass case she had never tried

E19.text: Mara Lisle told Ines Okafor she was the Cormorant, saying she drew the bird, saw boats come in at night when the table said the steps would be dry, and signed anonymously.

E20.text: Ines Okafor opened the tide-clock case on the tower landing with the fish-shaped brass key and found the missing Salt Ledger pages rolled and tied with twine behind the clock hand.
E20.quote: were the missing pages of the Salt Ledger

E21.text: The recovered pages, in Brandt's writing, recorded twenty-four barrels of salt monthly going from the warehouse to the outer steps, each entry marked with the names A. Pike and the Crane Company.
E21.quote: he had recorded twenty-four barrels of salt that went from the warehouse to the outer steps

Q11.text: Mara Lisle suggested Aldous Brandt found out about the barrels and then vanished, but where Brandt went and whether Pike was responsible was not stated.

W8.name: Aldous Brandt
W8.text: Aldous Brandt, the old keeper, was revealed to be alive: he escaped Pike's men in a skiff and was hidden by Tobiah Wren on the outer skerry.
W8.quote: When Pike's men came for him he had got away in a skiff

E22.text: Tobiah Wren returned on the equinox tide with Aldous Brandt, who had not left willingly or died but had been hidden three weeks in the light-keeper's hut.
E22.quote: Tobiah Wren came up the harbour steps on the morning of the market

E23.text: Mara Venn revealed she had taken Ines's tally to protect it from Pike and locked it in the council chest, which only her seal opens.
E23.quote: I carried it to the council chest, which only my seal opens.

E24.text: Dr Anselm Pike was taken at his press with false tide tables on the rack, and the council refused the Crane Company's offer.
E24.quote: Dr Pike was taken at his press

units.title: 7. The Door That Isn't a Door
